cards.headline: How to be a party-savvy parent when it comes to kids’ birthdays
bullets: Parents can opt for a quiet movie outing instead of a big birthday party for kids.
This saves parents from extensive party planning and noisy celebrations.
It also means less awkward small talk with other parents.
The writer found elaborate parties exhausting and expensive over the years.
Parents might feel pressured to throw big parties from the baby's first 100 days.

cards.headline: Archaeological study to be carried out at Adam Park, a WWII battlefield and prisoner-of-war camp
bullets: An archaeological study will happen at Adam Park, a World War II battlefield and POW camp.
A metal box found in 2013, possibly for ammunition, was left buried and may be dug up.
The site, with old colonial bungalows, will be used for serviced apartments.
Previous digs found over 1,000 items, including coins and military gear.

cards.headline: Nearly one in 10 commuters changed morning travel habits, easing peak-hour NEL crunch: Jeffrey Siow
bullets: Almost 1 in 10 commuters took free off-peak train rides, easing morning crowds.
The free off-peak travel scheme started December 27, 2025, on the North East Line.
Nine percent of commuters shifted travel times, resulting in less crowded trains.
Ten new bus services were added to serve the north-east corridor since May 2025.
Electricity prices may rise in July, but rebates will help households.

cards.headline: Cyclist dies after accident with tipper truck in Pasir Ris
bullets: A 35-year-old cyclist died after an accident with a tipper truck in Pasir Ris on May 23.
The accident happened around 4:30pm at the junction of Pasir Ris Drive 4 and Pasir Ris Drive 3.
The tipper truck driver, aged 29, is helping police with their ongoing investigations.
This comes as traffic deaths in Singapore reached a 10-year high last year.

cards.headline: Sustainable fun: June school holiday activities to keep kids busy while learning to save the earth
bullets: Museums and institutions offer free and ticketed activities from May 30 to June 28 for Children's Season.
A new book, Quiz Champs: Tackling Climate Change With Biogirl MJ, teaches kids about environmental issues.
Outdoor School Singapore offers camps like Water Trekkers and Wetland Wanderers for kids aged seven to nine.
These holiday activities aim to teach children about sustainability and their role in protecting the Earth.

cards.headline: Free morning off-peak train rides in northeast Singapore reduced crowding by 9%: Jeffrey Siow
bullets: Free off-peak train rides in northeast Singapore cut crowding by 9%.
The free rides apply to the North East Line and Sengkang-Punggol LRT during certain off-peak hours.
Public transport fares have not changed since the Middle East crisis began.
Government is watching the Middle East situation and may offer more support if needed.

cards.headline: Kim Lim says her nine-year-old son is ‘too kind’, worries he may be easily taken advantage of
bullets: Kim Lim worries her nine-year-old son Kyden is too kind and might be easily taken advantage of.
She prioritises Kyden's character and kindness over top academic results.
Kyden shows maturity by letting his younger cousins play with toys first.
Kim Lim jokes about regretting praying for her son to be kind.

cards.headline: Koh Poh Koon says he is ‘not running away’ at final event as senior minister of state
bullets: Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon is stepping down from his roles on June 1 for family reasons.
He assured attendees at an event that he is not running away and will continue to be around.
Dr Koh also announced a new accreditation framework for Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioners and services.
A joint initiative for TCM and Healthier SG GPs to co-manage patient health will also be launched.

cards.headline: MediSave withdrawal limit for HIV drugs to go up from S$550 to S$850 monthly
bullets: MediSave withdrawals for HIV drugs will increase from S$550 to S$850 monthly starting June 1.
Family members can now use their MediSave accounts to help pay for HIV treatments.
In 2025, 166 new HIV cases were reported, a slight rise from the previous year.
HIV self-testing kits have seen strong demand, with over 800 sold monthly since January.

cards.headline: 'Find a moment for yourself': Why Singaporean artist Amanda Heng is inviting people to just rest in Venice
bullets: Singaporean artist Amanda Heng created an art installation called 'A Pause' at the Venice Biennale.
The installation invites visitors to slow down and find a moment for themselves.
It features wide wooden steps and large windows for rest and reflection.
Heng's work explores the idea of rest and the ageing body.

cards.headline: Showdown at Tanglin Club sees new rival slate elected to general committee
bullets: Tanglin Club members elected a new committee due to concerns over spending and governance.
The new committee aims for better consultation on club projects like pickleball courts.
Members approved raising the annual term membership entrance fee to S$10,500.
Spending plans include S$7 million for green building certification and S$5 million for pickleball courts.

cards.headline: US mortgage rates hit highest since August as war fans inflation
bullets: US mortgage rates are now at 6.51%, the highest since August.
This is the biggest weekly jump in mortgage rates since late March.
Rising oil prices from the Iran war are pushing up inflation and bond yields.
Despite higher rates, US home sales have shown surprising strength.
Buyers are still paying less than the 6.86% rate seen last year.

cards.headline: Guardiola to end decade-long Man City reign at end of season
bullets: Pep Guardiola is leaving Manchester City after ten years as their manager.
He has won six Premier League titles, three FA Cups, and the Champions League with the club.
Guardiola said it is his time to leave, but he has no specific reason.
His final game in charge will be against Aston Villa this Sunday.

cards.headline: European champions Spain on quest to regain World Cup crown
bullets: Spain are favourites to win the World Cup after winning Euro 2024.
France, who lost the last final, are expected to reach the semi-finals.
Norway returns to the World Cup with star striker Erling Haaland.
Iran could face the US in the next round if group results go their way.
Cape Verde and Iraq are making their World Cup debuts.

cards.headline: Elderly woman allegedly hit by car along Yishun Ring Road, witnesses saw pool of blood
bullets: An elderly woman was hit by a car on Yishun Ring Road.
The accident happened around 9am on May 23.
Witnesses saw a pool of blood at the scene.
One person was taken to Khoo Teck Phuat Hospital.

cards.headline: M'sian parents identify son, 4, in viral abuse video, leading to babysitter's arrest
bullets: Malaysian parents identified their four-year-old son in a viral abuse video.
The video showed a woman hitting the boy at the back of a house.
Police arrested a 60-year-old babysitter in Seremban after the parents reported the incident.
The boy had reportedly been with the babysitter for seven months.

cards.headline: S'pore man who cleaned stranger's vomit on MRT recognised by Public Transport Council for caring act
bullets: A young man cleaned up a stranger's vomit on the MRT train.
His kind act on the North-East line was filmed and went viral.
The Public Transport Council met him to thank him for his caring act.
He has also been nominated for the Caring Commuter Award.

cards.headline: 13 Upcoming Live Performances in 2026 – Concerts, Comedies & Musicals In Singapore
bullets: The musical Charlie and the Chocolate Factory runs from May 19 to June 7 at Marina Bay Sands.
Singapore Chinese Orchestra will hold a children's concert about music and weather from May 22 to 26.
Comedian Kumar will perform shows about the World Cup and life from June 25 to July 12.
Singer The Kid LAROI performs his A Perfect World Tour on July 1 at Arena @ Expo.
The musical Legally Blonde opens July 29 at the Esplanade Theatre.

Run 8km and get a free soup set at The Soup Spoon's Kallang Wave Mall outlet.
